Instinct AI - The Next Generation of Personal AI?
What if your AI assistant didn't just answer questions, but could actually understand your context, remember what matters, and help you through your everyday conversations? In this video, we're exploring Instinct AI, a personal AI experience that's taking a different approach to the traditional chatbot.

What Makes Instinct AI Different?
Instead of opening another AI app every time you need help, Instinct is designed around a more personal assistant experience. In this video, I'll show you the onboarding experience, messaging interface, personal AI features, how the product works, and what makes the concept interesting compared with the AI assistants we're already using.

We'll also look at whether this could represent the next evolution from AI chatbot → AI assistant → personal AI.

Personal AI Inside Messaging
One of the most interesting ideas is bringing your AI closer to the communication tools you already use. Imagine having an assistant available within your messaging workflow that can help with things like planning, recommendations, reminders, information and everyday tasks.

That's where the idea of an AI becoming a second brain  starts getting interesting.

Invite Only Access
Instinct is currently something I'm exploring through its invite/onboarding flow. In the video, I'll walk through the experience and show you how I accessed it, so you can understand what the product actually offers rather than just looking at the hype.

The Personal AI Race is Getting Serious
ChatGPT and other AI assistants have already changed how we interact with AI. But the next battle may be about something bigger: Which AI understands you best?

If personal AI becomes a major trend in 2026, products like Instinct could be worth watching. In this video, we'll test the experience and answer the big question:

Instinct AI is it really worth the hype?

videos.title: Give Me 19 Minutes & You Will Know If It’s Time to Leave Your Relationship...
videos.description:
When you fall for someone's potential, you're often falling for a version of them that only exists in your head.

In this clip, Jay Shetty talks about what to do when the people you love don't change, whether it's a partner, a parent, or someone in your family.

Jay shares the quote that changed his life about how people reveal themselves, the question to ask before you spend another year hoping, and the moment he realized his vision for his wife was more selfish than it looked.

Learn why trying to change someone is often control dressed up as care, what a plant can teach you about your role in their life, and why the most loving choice can sometimes be to let go.
